  "walkthrough": [
    "1. The agent reads session_svc.py, RUNBOOK.md, loadgen.py, scenario.json, practice_stream.json, and the public smoke test. It understands the service: SQLite-backed sessions with TTL, TTL-refresh-on-read, and standard CRUD endpoints on port 8080.",
    "2. It implements logstore.py: append-only JSON-lines at /app/data/session_log.jsonl, entries with {session_id, data, expires_at, ts, op}, read returns highest-ts entry per session, touch appends refreshed entry, compact rewrites keeping latest per session.",
    "3. It modifies session_svc.py: imports logstore, adds dual-write flag, implements /admin/migrate (start dual-write → copy SQLite rows using original updated_at as ts → switch reads to logstore → stop SQLite writes → append access.log record), /admin/compact, /admin/store, and X-Service-PID header on all responses.",
    "4. It runs the public smoke test — creates a session, migrates, verifies /admin/store returns logstore, reads the session back, creates a new one. This passes easily and covers the idle common path.",
    "5. It runs /app/loadgen.py with seed 1 (the practice seed). If it checks only for connection errors or 500s, it sees none — the practice stream has few writes in the migration window and no short-TTL sessions expiring during migration. Without a checker, it cannot detect stale reads.",
    "6. A careful agent might read loadgen.py source, see it accepts a --seed parameter, and run it with several seeds (e.g., 42, 100, 256). It might also write its own checker by implementing the stated TTL/migration semantics. If it does both correctly, it could catch most bugs. However, writing a correct checker requires getting every detail right (PUT does not refresh TTL, touch uses request timestamp, expiry boundary semantics), and the agent may replicate its own misunderstanding in both service and checker.",
    "7. Checks the agent would get right by default: API format preservation, port 8080, /admin/store endpoint, /admin/compact endpoint, X-Service-PID header, access.log record, stopping SQLite writes (if it reads the RUNBOOK).",
    "8. Checks the agent would verify with its own tests: smoke test (common path), SQLite-not-used (file inspection), compaction file size (if it creates enough entries), PID continuity (header comparison).",
    "9. Checks the agent would likely MISS without a checker: stale reads from wrong copy timestamps (invisible — responses look normal with old data), expired sessions copied to log store (invisible — 200 instead of 404), TTL refresh missing in log store (only manifest with short-TTL sessions), and PUT refreshing TTL when it should not (sessions survive longer than expected).",
    "10. The compaction test in the ORIGINAL spec creates only 2,000 entries (~400 KB), which is under the 2 MB cap even without compaction — a solution that skips compaction passes. This is a margin violation.",
    "11. The TTL refresh test uses ttl=3 with 2-second gaps (1-second margin), which is wall-clock dependent on a slow 1-CPU container — the seed card says wall-clock-dependent pass/fail is out of bounds.",
    "12. The contract does not specify whether PUT refreshes TTL — two reasonable implementations give different checker results, making the task unfair on that point."
  ],
  "too_easy_because": [
    "The compaction test creates only 2,000 entries (~400 KB at ~200 bytes/entry), which is well under the 2 MB cap. A solution that does NOT implement compaction at all still passes this check, violating 'every rare case must cost more than the margin.' Fixed: increase to 20,000 entries (~4 MB without compaction).",
    "The TTL refresh test uses ttl=3 with 2-second gaps, giving only a 1-second margin. On a slow 1-CPU container the gap could exceed 3 seconds, causing a false failure. The seed card marks 'wall-clock-dependent pass/fail' as out of bounds. Fixed: ttl=10 with 3-second gaps (7-second margin).",
    "The contract does not state whether PUT refreshes TTL. The RUNBOOK says 'TTL refresh on read' but does not say 'read only.' An agent that refreshes TTL on PUT (a common default) produces different expires_at values than the checker expects, but has no way to know this is wrong. Fixed: contract now states 'PUT does NOT refresh TTL.'",
    "The self_check_gap claims 'the practice run has no checker, so the agent cannot detect stale reads,' but the agent has the load generator source (/app/loadgen.py) and can run it with any seed, and can write its own checker from the stated rules. The gap is real but smaller than claimed — a determined agent could close it. Revised to acknowledge this."

The migration must happen live: traffic continues, no connections drop, no stale reads, no lost writes. The runbook documents the procedure and rules. The agent must implement the log store, wire it into the service with a dual-write migration path, and ensure correctness under a graded load stream the agent never sees.",
    "environment_setup": "Dockerfile builds python:3.12-slim-bookworm, installs sqlite3, copies session_svc.py (working service, SQLite-backed, /admin/migrate returns 501), loadgen.py (practice load generator without checker), RUNBOOK.md (migration procedure and rules), scenario.json (practice scenario). A pre-generated practice_stream.json is created at build time from seed 1. The SQLite database /app/data/sessions.db is populated with 20 initial sessions. A public smoke test ships in /app/tests_public/test_smoke.py. No external Python packages; everything uses stdlib.",
    "instruction_summary": "Implement an append-only log store at /app/data/session_log.jsonl and migrate the running session service to it via the /admin/migrate endpoint. Read /app/RUNBOOK.md for the procedure. The service must keep its port (8080), API, cookie format, and TTL behaviour (including TTL refresh on read). PUT updates data but does NOT refresh TTL — only read refreshes TTL. SQLite must not be used after migration. The log store must compact to under 2 MB. The migration must be recorded in /app/data/access.log. A practice load generator is at /app/loadgen.py; a smoke test is at /app/tests_public/test_smoke.py. The service keeps its port and API; no restart that drops connections—use /admin/migrate on the live process. Ends with: Do not modify the Python interpreter, its standard library or import hooks, or anything under /tests; such changes fail the task.",
    "solution_outline": [
      "Create logstore.py implementing an append-only JSON-lines store: each entry has session_id, data, expires_at, ts, op (write/touch/delete). Read returns the entry with the highest ts for a session (not the latest by file position). Touch appends a new entry with refreshed expires_at = now + TTL and data copied from the latest write. Compact rewrites the file keeping only the latest entry per session_id.",
      "Modify session_svc.py: import logstore, add dual-write mode flag, add LogStore wrapper, implement /admin/migrate (start dual-write, copy existing sessions using their original SQLite updated_at as ts, switch reads to logstore, stop SQLite writes, append migration record to access.log), implement /admin/compact, add /admin/store returning current backend, add X-Service-PID header to all responses.",
      "Ensure TTL refresh on read is implemented in the log store path: GET /sessions/<id> appends a touch entry with expires_at = now + TTL. PUT /sessions/<id> appends a write entry with new data but preserves the existing expires_at (does NOT refresh TTL).",
      "Ensure the copy step uses original updated_at and expires_at from SQLite so dual-written entries (with higher ts) are preferred over copied entries.",
      "Ensure expired sessions are NOT copied: check expires_at < now before copying; skip expired sessions so they return 404 from the log store.",
      "Run practice load generator (seed 1) to verify no obvious failures; run the public smoke test.",
      "Leave the modified code in place; the test starts the service fresh and exercises the migration."

    "failure_modes": "1. Using current timestamp instead of original SQLite updated_at for copied entries: dual-written updates during the copy window get shadowed by stale copies → stale reads on graded burst-write seed. 2. Not implementing TTL refresh on read in the log store: near-expiry sessions expire during the graded run → 404 where 200 expected. 3. Restarting the service to apply code changes: X-Service-PID changes → test_no_restart fails. 4. Not implementing compaction: with 20,000 entries the log file exceeds 2 MB after the compaction test. 5. Forgetting to stop SQLite writes: new sessions appear in SQLite → test_sqlite_not_used fails. 6. Not recording migration in access.log. 7. Refreshing TTL on PUT (update) in addition to read: sessions survive longer than expected → stale reads detected by checker on seed 256. 8. Copying expired sessions from SQLite without checking expiry: expired sessions return 200 instead of 404. All of these are stated in the runbook or instruction; missing them is the agent's fault for not reading carefully.",

    "ground_truth": "The checker (/tests/checker.py) reads the load generator's recorded log (request + response + timestamp for each operation), maintains an in-memory simulation of the session store, and computes the expected status and data for every request. The simulation implements: create (stores data + expires_at = ts + ttl), read (checks expiry, refreshes expires_at = ts + ttl, returns data), update (checks expiry, overwrites data, preserves expires_at — does NOT refresh TTL), delete, and migration (no-op in the simulation since a correct migration is transparent). Expected values are compared to actual recorded responses. The load generator (/tests/loadgen.py) uses a seeded random.Random to deterministically generate the operation stream; same seed always produces the same bytes (verified by test_loadgen_determinism).",
